Technical writing.
Full text guide.

All 10 lessons, examples, and practice exercises. This version works without JavaScript and can be printed.

  1. Start with the reader

Lesson 1 / Foundations

Start with the reader

Technical writing helps someone understand a subject or complete a task. Start by deciding who that someone is.

Technical writing communicates specialized knowledge in a usable form. It appears in software guides, assembly instructions, procedures, proposals, and reports. The subject can be engineering, business, the arts, or any field with specialized methods.

Keep the language clear. Adjust the detail.

A first-time user and a repair technician need different information about the same product. Use familiar words for both. Change the depth, prerequisites, and examples to match their work.

For a new user

Connect the printer to the same Wi-Fi network as your laptop.

For a technician

Check the printer’s network configuration and confirm that its IP address is reachable from the client subnet.

Before you draft

  1. Name the reader and the task.
  2. List what the reader already knows.
  3. Identify what they need next.
  4. Choose a format that makes that information easy to find.

Practice

A new teammate needs to run your project locally. Write down what they know, what they need installed, and what a successful first run looks like.

Show a sample answer

For a teammate who knows Git but has never used this project: list the required runtime version, how to install dependencies, how to start the app, and the page or message they should see. Explain project-specific terms.

Keep this rule

Match the information to the reader’s task, while keeping the language clear.

Lesson 2 / Foundations

Build a useful definition

A good definition tells the reader what something is, where it belongs, and what makes it distinct.

Term+Class+Distinguishing detail

Give each part a job

The term names the thing. The class places it in a recognizable group. The distinguishing detail separates it from other members of that group.

A password manager is an application that stores login credentials and helps you retrieve them securely.

term / class / distinguishing detail

Choose the narrowest useful class

“Application” gives the reader more information than “thing.” A useful category should be familiar and accurate. Avoid defining a word with itself: “A compiler is something that compiles” offers little help.

Add distinguishing details that matter to the reader. A long list of incidental features makes the definition harder to use.

Practice

Define a backup in one sentence. Include the term, a class, and a detail that explains its purpose.

Show a sample answer

A backup is a copy of data kept so it can be restored if the original is lost or damaged. “Copy of data” is the class; the restoration purpose distinguishes it from an arbitrary duplicate.

Keep this rule

Define with a recognizable category and a meaningful difference.

Lesson 3 / Foundations

Choose the right category

Class words give readers a starting point. Choose one that explains the object without forcing it into an artificial box.

The transcript introduces physical and digital class words. Treat these as useful vocabulary, rather than mutually exclusive scientific categories. A pair of scissors can be both a tool and a mechanism.

Useful class words
CategoryWhat it helps describeExample
ToolAn object used to do workScrewdriver
InstrumentAn object used for measurement, observation, or a specialized activityThermometer
ApparatusEquipment or a setup used for a purposeLaboratory distillation setup
MachineA system of parts that performs workSewing machine
MechanismAn arrangement that transmits or controls motionLock mechanism
EngineA machine that converts energy into mechanical workCombustion engine
ApplianceEquipment designed for a particular household or similar taskMicrowave oven
GadgetAn informal name for a small, useful deviceFitness tracker
DeviceA broad term that benefits from a qualifierElectronic calculator
HardwarePhysical computer componentsKeyboard
SoftwarePrograms and related instructionsOperating system
ApplicationSoftware designed for a taskPhoto editor
PlatformAn environment that supports services or applicationsLearning platform
Cloud serviceComputing resources accessed over a networkHosted storage service

Categories overlap and meanings depend on the field. Machines do not all need gears, and cloud computing includes more than storage. Verify the definition for your actual subject.

Practice

Choose a useful class for a code editor. Then explain why “software” alone might be too broad for a beginner.

Show a sample answer

A code editor is an application for writing and editing source code. “Software” is accurate, but “application” plus its purpose gives a beginner a more useful picture.

Keep this rule

Use categories to help comprehension, and check where their boundaries overlap.

Lesson 4 / Foundations

Make the meaning concrete

A one-sentence definition is a starting point. Add the detail your reader needs to picture it or tell it apart.

Seven ways to expand a definition

  1. Assign a class. A barometer is an instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure.
  2. Describe its form. Explain shape, size, or arrangement when appearance matters.
  3. Explain the word’s origin. Use a verified root word if it helps the meaning stick.
  4. Move from general to specific. Define the broad concept, then introduce relevant types.
  5. Offer familiar wording. Explain a specialist term in everyday language without losing precision.
  6. Compare and contrast. Explain a shared purpose and a useful difference.
  7. Give an example. Show one recognizable instance of the concept.
Example: compare and contrast

A local backup stays on a device you control. A cloud backup stores a copy with a remote service. Both support recovery, but their access and failure conditions differ.

Choose the methods that answer a real question. You do not need all seven in every definition.

Practice

Explain a browser cache using a definition, familiar wording, and one concrete example.

Show a sample answer

A browser cache is local storage for copies of website resources. It helps the browser reuse files it has already downloaded. For example, it may reuse a site’s logo instead of downloading it again on every page.

Keep this rule

Expand a definition with examples and distinctions that help this reader.

Lesson 5 / Explain and instruct

Describe an object

Help the reader recognize the object, understand its parts, and see how those parts work together.

Use four layers

  1. Identity and purpose. Define the object and say what it does.
  2. Appearance. Show its shape and arrangement with a labeled diagram when useful.
  3. Components. Describe the relevant parts in a consistent order.
  4. Operation. Explain how the parts work together.

A USB flash drive is a portable storage device. Its connector links it to a compatible port. The controller manages transfers between the computer and the memory chip, where data is stored.

Keep the description easy to follow

Use the same labels in the diagram and text. Choose an order—such as left to right or input to output—and stay with it. Include dimensions, materials, or specifications only when relevant and verified.

Practice

Describe a keyboard in four short parts: purpose, appearance, components, and operation.

Show a sample answer

Purpose: enter text and commands. Appearance: a board of labeled keys. Components: keys, switches or sensors, a controller, and a connection. Operation: pressing a key sends an input signal to the connected device. Adapt the details to the keyboard model.

Keep this rule

Describe purpose, appearance, parts, and operation in a consistent order.

Lesson 6 / Explain and instruct

Put notices before the risk

A useful notice explains what could happen and what the reader should do before they reach that point.

Notices call attention to information that affects a task. Place each notice beside the relevant step, before the reader encounters the hazard or consequence.

Note

Add helpful context: “Large exports may take several minutes.”

Caution · illustrative data example

Exporting to an existing filename may replace your earlier file. Choose a new filename to keep both versions.

Write the consequence and the action

“Be careful” is too vague. Name the specific issue and the step that avoids it. Keep the notice short enough to read at the point of action.

Use the applicable notice system

The transcript teaches note, caution, warning, and danger with colored boxes. Those definitions and colors are a course convention, not a universal safety standard. For equipment or safety documentation, use the applicable standard and manufacturer’s guidance.

Keep a visible text label. Color alone should never carry the notice’s meaning. Place essential notices in the main flow rather than hiding them in a collapsed panel.

Practice

Write a notice for a step that overwrites an existing configuration file. Include the consequence and a way to preserve the old version.

Show a sample answer

Caution: This step replaces config.json. Save a copy of your current config.json before continuing if you need to keep its settings. The notice belongs before the replacement step.

Keep this rule

Place a specific consequence and preventive action before the relevant step.

Lesson 7 / Explain and instruct

Write steps people can follow

Give readers a clear starting point, one useful action at a time, and a way to recognize the result.

A manual may include product background, operating instructions, notices, troubleshooting, and support information. A single procedure should focus on a specific task.

Start each step with an action

Indirect

The file is selected by the operator, who then initiates the export process.

Imperative

Select the file. Choose Export.

The imperative is the command form of a verb: select, open, connect, save. It speaks directly to the reader without repeating “you” in every sentence.

Illustrative procedure · export a document

Before you start: Open the document in an editor that supports PDF export.

  1. Open the File menu.
  2. Choose Export, then select PDF.
  3. Choose a folder and enter a filename.
  4. Select Save.
  5. Open the PDF and check that its pages display correctly.

Check the sequence

Use numbered steps for order, descriptive subheadings for phases, and labeled images when they clarify an action. Match menu labels to the real product. State prerequisites and place notices before consequential actions.

Practice

Rewrite: “The user should now proceed to the settings area, where the notification preferences can be modified.”

Show a sample answer

Open Settings. Select Notifications. Choose the notifications you want to receive. Add the exact save action if this interface requires one.

Keep this rule

Lead with verbs, follow the task’s order, and make the result observable.

Lesson 8 / Explain and instruct

Explain how a process works

Make the starting conditions, stages, and result visible. Decide whether you are explaining the process or directing someone through it.

A process description explains what happens and why. A procedure tells someone what to do. The transcript combines these approaches; choose the one that fits the reader’s purpose.

Give the process a clear boundary

  1. Define its purpose and outcome.
  2. List inputs, materials, or prerequisites.
  3. Describe the stages in order.
  4. Explain important changes between stages.
  5. State the final result and relevant checks.
Input

Source document

Transformation

PDF export

Output

Shareable PDF

Description

During export, the editor converts the document’s content and layout into a PDF. The resulting file can be opened in a PDF reader.

Instruction

Choose Export, select PDF, and save the file.

For a hands-on process, include the materials, numbered actions, diagrams, and notices needed to carry it out. Follow equipment-specific guidance rather than treating a generic description as an operating manual.

Practice

Write one sentence explaining what happens during a software build, then one sentence telling a developer how to start this project’s build.

Show a sample answer

Description: The build process transforms the project’s source files into distributable output. Instruction: Run the documented build command from the project folder. Replace that generic phrase with the verified command for the actual project.

Keep this rule

Separate what happens from what the reader must do.

Lesson 9 / Reports

Choose a report’s purpose

Decide whether the report needs to present information, interpret findings, or recommend an action.

A report organizes information for a reader and a purpose. It may use original observations, existing sources, or both. Cite the sources and distinguish evidence from interpretation.

The transcript’s functional categories
PurposeWhat it includesIllustrative example
InformationalFactsFive delivery businesses operate in this area.
ExaminationalFacts and interpretationFive businesses operate here; the available financial data suggests limited profitability.
AnalyticalFacts, interpretation, and a recommendationCompare demand and costs in another area before deciding where to expand.

“Examinational” is the transcript’s label. Terminology varies across organizations; analytical reports do not always require a recommendation.

Other useful ways to classify reports

  • Subject: engineering, finance, research, or another field.
  • Frequency: recurring or prepared for a particular assignment.
  • Formality: a brief internal update or a formal submission.
  • Format: memo, letter, short report, or longer document.
  • Relationship: internal, prepared by an outside specialist, or intended for a public audience.

The required format depends on your organization, assignment, and readers. Confirm those constraints before drafting.

Practice

A manager asks which hosting option the team should choose. What must the report include beyond a list of prices?

Show a sample answer

Compare the options against the team’s requirements, explain the evidence and tradeoffs, and make a recommendation with its assumptions and limits. Price alone does not answer which option fits.

Keep this rule

Let the reader’s decision determine the report’s evidence and structure.

Lesson 10 / Reports

Build a report people can use

Give readers a short route to the answer and enough supporting detail to assess how you reached it.

Front matter

Title, contents, lists of figures or tables, executive summary

Main body

Introduction, context, methods, findings, discussion, conclusions

Back matter

References, appendices, supporting material

Set up the main body

Introduce the purpose, scope, background, and limitations. Explain how the information was collected. Present the findings, then show how they support the conclusions. Add recommendations when the task calls for them.

For a survey, describe the participants, recruitment, questions, collection period, and analysis. Explain sampling limits. A large response count alone does not establish a representative sample or prove a hypothesis.

Make evidence traceable

Use descriptive headings that match the table of contents. Label tables and figures consistently and explain what each shows. Include sources and enough method detail to help readers judge the findings.

Write the executive summary last

Answer three questions: Why was the report prepared? How was the work done? What did it find? Include the main recommendation if one is required. The executive summary covers the report as a whole; the closing summary revisits the findings and conclusions.

Illustrative executive summary

This report compares two hosting options for the documentation site. The comparison uses published pricing, a test deployment, and the team’s maintenance requirements. Both options support the current site; option A is recommended for its simpler deployment process. The comparison excludes future traffic growth and paid support.

Front and back matter help readers navigate and verify a report. Their exact order, pagination, summary length, and required headings depend on the assignment or house style.

Practice

Draft a three-sentence executive summary for a report you might write: purpose, method, and finding. Keep any recommendation tied to evidence.

Show a sample answer

Example: This report investigates slow local setup for new contributors. It reviews the setup guide and records three observed onboarding sessions. Missing prerequisites caused repeated failures, so the report recommends adding a tested prerequisite checklist. These are illustrative findings, not research conducted for this site.

Keep this rule

Lead with the answer, then make the evidence and its limits easy to inspect.
